name: Marriage Exemption Certificate (spousal work-permit exemption)

requirements.blocker_text: Married to a Jamaican citizen -- exempts the foreign spouse from needing a standard work permit.

outcome.duration_length: 3 years for an expatriate male spouse of a Jamaican citizen; for an expatriate female spouse, valid for the duration of the marriage -- an asymmetry sourced directly from MLSS's own page, likely a legacy artifact of the 1964 Exemptions Regulations not yet updated, disclosed rather than smoothed over

sources.title: Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MLSS), Jamaica -- Marriage Exemption Certificate: fee JMD 17,250; validity 3 years for an expatriate male spouse, 'for the duration of the marriage' for an expatriate female spouse of a Jamaican citizen

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Jamaica). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- tier-1 MLSS sourced. GENDERED STRUCTURAL ASYMMETRY, SOURCED DIRECTLY FROM THE PRIMARY GOVERNMENT PAGE AS-IS: the certificate's stated validity period differs by the sex of the FOREIGN spouse (3 years fixed for a man, indefinite for the duration of the marriage for a woman) -- this reads as inconsistent with modern equal-treatment norms and likely reflects legacy language from the 1964 Foreign Nationals and Commonwealth Citizens (Employment) Exemptions Regulations that hasn't been updated, but it is what MLSS's own current page states, so it is reported as found rather than smoothed into a symmetric rule. No dedicated 'family reunification visa' distinct from this exemption certificate, the permanent-residence spousal/dependent categories (see jm_permanent_residence.json), or citizenship registration by marriage (see jm_citizenship_by_marriage.json) was found -- Jamaica routes family-based status through these three mechanisms rather than a single unified family visa.
